view: This is the first full quarter after the May CSRC action. Under the stock's 61% fall this year, the Q3 picture is a sequential step-down that Futu has already shown and that TIGR has already traded on. Scaled from Futu, Tiger's total revenue lands around $165-172M against $182.3M in Q2, with commissions down and interest income only slightly lower. That is near or a little under the stale, inconsistent consensus. Futu's own Q3 shows the market treated that kind of step-down as known: revenue beat, EPS slightly missed, and the stock rose. Small positives that could move the headline: the non-deductible penalty tax treatment that management said it expects to start reversing in H2, the Q2 severance that will not recur, the $50M buyback against a ~5x P/E, and the company's own guide of flat-to-up funded accounts. Risks: end-of-September client assets probably fell with markets (Futu -4.6% QoQ), funded-account growth may slip as Futu's did, and the 8:00 ET call's Q4-to-date commentary falls inside a weak October and November tape. FUTU itself fell from about $114 to $83 between late September and 11-18. TIGR's history inside a bmo window leans toward an intraday fade. Q2 2026 opened -4.7% and closed -0.1%, then fell -7.3% the next day. Q4 2025 traded down to -7.1% intraday and closed -3.1%. Q3 2025 opened +8.5% and closed +4.0%. Q2 2025 closed -9.8% and Q1 2025 closed -3.8%. The last outlier up was Q4 2024 at +21.6%. Nothing I found is both Tiger-specific and newer than the Futu read the price already holds, so I see no reaction I could call unpriced. I lean slightly down on the fade pattern and on downside skew.

recommendation.reason: The decisive datapoint for Tiger's quarter is Futu's Q3: a 22% sequential volume drop and a 7% revenue drop. It was published on 11-19 and TIGR traded on it the same day (+7.4%). Consensus for TIGR is thin and internally inconsistent, so a headline beat or miss cannot be read reliably beforehand. The Q2 'beat' against a $153.9M estimate still drew an intraday sell-off. I can name no mechanism with evidence the price lacks, so I am not recommending.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 new funded accounts well above 32.6k with client assets held near $60B or above, or a larger buyback or dividend. Against a ~5x P/E, either could carry the stock up through 13:00 ET instead of the usual fade.

self_critique: A cheap, heavily shorted-in-sentiment stock with a call-heavy open-interest book could pop on any clean headline: GAAP EPS helped by the penalty tax reversal, flat-to-up funded accounts, or a bigger buyback. TIGR also did gap +8.5% on Q3 2025. The other way, the fade pattern rests on six prints, and Futu's slower funded-account growth plus weak October-November markets could make the Q4 commentary a clear negative. Neither side is strong enough to move me off a near-coin-flip.
approach_notes: P4's 'show it is priced' was useful: the peer read could be tied directly to TIGR's own price move on Futu's print day. P3's alternative-source ideas paid little for a foreign broker with no monthly disclosures, and the stale, inconsistent consensus made the 'stale estimate' bias impossible to exploit either way.
